title: What the Unearned Premium on a Given-Up Plan Is Set Against
content:
What the unearned premium on a given-up Pass and Trip Protection plan is set against is settled from the
standing of the covered holding under the Season Pass Programme and from what that holding's account shows.

1. Where the covered holding's account carries an instalment the payment method refused in the season,
   everything standing unpaid on the protection account, premium and charges alike, is set against the
   unearned premium.
2. Where the covered holding's account carries no refused instalment in the season and the covered holding's
   record shows it given up in the season, nothing at all is set against the unearned premium, what stands
   unpaid on the plan being dealt with on the covered holding's own settlement.
3. In every other case only the charges standing unpaid on the protection account are set against the unearned
   premium, the premium standing unpaid being left on the schedule it rides on.

**Reading the ladder.** The three are read in the order given. A refused instalment on the covered holding's
account within the season brings the whole of what stands unpaid into the reckoning, whatever the holding's
standing. Only where no such instalment stands does the holding's own standing come into it, and then a
covered holding given up in the season takes everything off the reckoning.

**Worked cases (hypothetical inputs).** A plan whose protection account carries 160.00 USD standing unpaid, of
which 25.00 USD is charges, and whose covered holding's account shows one instalment refused in the season:
160.00 USD is set against the unearned premium. The same plan with no refused instalment and a covered holding
given up in the season: nothing at all is set against it. The same plan with no refused instalment and a
covered holding still standing: 25.00 USD is set against it.
